frameworks.name: Optionality vs. Commitment Trade-Off
frameworks.definition: The principle that choosing commitment in any domain (relationships, locations, business strategy) requires eliminating alternative options; maximum optionality is incompatible with the rewards of deep commitment.

frameworks.name: Zero to 100M Scaling Roadmap
frameworks.definition: A 10-stage revenue progression (zero to 100M+) with defined constraints and solution steps across eight business functions, validated across software, physical products, services, and brick-and-mortar.

claims.text: Having a relationship while building a business is presented as "difficult" but is not harder than being in a relationship while not working on a business; the real constraint is that you have less time in both scenarios, not that one path eliminates the other.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Both activities (building a business, maintaining a relationship) are time-consuming, so the combined load is the same either way — the perception of impossibility comes from narrative rather than constraint.

claims.text: Commitment is defined as the elimination of alternatives; if ultimate optionality is the primary goal, a lifelong partner is incompatible with that goal.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Maximizing options in any domain (e.g., choosing where to live to access mountains, valleys, deserts, and snow all simultaneously) is mathematically impossible; at some point, the goal shifts from option-maximization to option-selection, requiring tradeoff acceptance.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: No single location satisfies all environment preferences; the gain from commitment (actual residence) requires the loss of optionality (access to all environments). The metaphor applies to relationships, career paths, and business decisions.
bounded_by: Does not apply to situations where true alternatives exist that satisfy all constraints (rare in practice).

claims.text: The societal narrative pushes maximum optionality and freedom, framing commitment as a constraint rather than a choice with trade-offs.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Pursuing anything difficult in life (business, relationships, skill mastery) requires accepting that it is not convenient; the question is whether the outcome justifies the inconvenience.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Alex Hormozi has built a 10-stage revenue roadmap from zero to 100 million dollars (and beyond) that applies across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar models; fewer than 1% of companies complete all stages.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Applies to companies across multiple business models (software, products, services, retail).

numbers.axis: company completion rate across the 10-stage roadmap

claims.text: The roadmap breaks down the constraint (what creates bottlenecks), the symptoms (how to recognize the constraint), and solution steps across eight business functions at each stage.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

examples.text: Alex Hormozi and his partner built their lives together, refuting the narrative that a relationship necessarily prevents business success. The example illustrates that the trade-off is not between "business or relationship" but between time allocation across both commitments.

A person cannot simultaneously choose to live in mountains, valleys, deserts, and snowy climates unless they move continuously (which nullifies the benefit of living anywhere). This illustrates the maximal-optionality problem: the gain from commitment requires the loss of alternative paths.

practices.text: When deciding on a major commitment (relationship, business focus, location), explicitly surface and accept the specific trades you are making rather than pretending the commitment has no cost.
Evaluate any major life decision (pursuing a business, starting a relationship) by asking: 'Is the outcome worth the inconvenience?' rather than seeking a path with no friction.
Use the 10-stage roadmap (available at acquisition.com/roadmap) as a diagnostic tool to identify which stage your company is at and what constraints you should expect.
